subject: digitsuface function placing surface semilandmarks undesirably

messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: digitsuface function placing surface semilandmarks undesirably
parts:
Hi, I am doing GMM on 3D dataset. I digitized a template using IDAV Landmark Editor. In this template, there are 5 landmarks, 20 curve semilandmarks, and 50 surface semilandmarks (Template_lmclmslm.nts file).

 

The following code can be used to view my template:

library(geomorph)

 

template_ply <- read.ply("C:\\Users\\<username>\\Desktop\\Template_vertices.ply")

lmks_template <- readland.nts("C:\\Users\\<username>\\Desktop\\Template_lmclmslm.nts")

 

plot3d(lmks_template[1:6,,1], type = "s", radius = 1.5, col = "red", aspect = FALSE, add = T)

plot3d(lmks_template[7:26,,1], type = "s", radius = 1.5, col = "blue", aspect = FALSE, add = T)

plot3d(lmks_template[27:76,,1], type = "s", radius = 1.5, col = "yellow", aspect = FALSE, add = T)

 

The resultant image is displayed as below (red landmarks, blue curve semilandmars, and yellow surface semilandmarks):

 

 

 

I wish to apply this template to my sample to let digitsurface function place surface semilandmarks on the sample for me. To accomplish this task, I used the following code:

open3d()

sample_ply <- read.ply("C:\\Users\\<username>\\Desktop\\Sample_vertices.ply")

lmks_sample <- readland.nts("C:\\Users\\<username>\\Desktop\\Sample_lmclm.nts")

digitsurface(sample_ply, fixed = lmks_sample[,,1], ptsize = 1, center = TRUE)

 

Note that lmks_sample[,,1] contains 6 landmarks and 20 curve semilandmarks. But I treat all 26 points as fixed landmarks at this stage. They will only be differentiated during GPA. I did it this way because geomorph tutorial allowed this.


Unfortunately, the resultant images is shown as below, which indicates that the semilandmarks are not placed in similar locations as they are placed in the template. Even the landmarks (red) of the sample are severely displaced.


 

I double checked the correctness of the landmarks of my sample using the following code:

open3d()

plot3d(sample_ply)

plot3d(lmks_sample[1:6,,1], type = "s", radius = 1.5, col = "red", aspect = FALSE, add = T)

plot3d(lmks_sample[7:26,,1], type = "s", radius = 1.5, col = "blue", aspect = FALSE, add = T)

 

The resultant image is shown below:

 

 

All landmarks (including real fixed landmarks and curve semilandmarks which are treated as fixed landmarks) are correctly positioned, suggesting that there should be no issue with the lmks_sample data fed to the fixed argument in digitsurface function.

 

I checked previous posts in this forum and noted two possible causes:

1. Lou indicated that "lumps of triangle summits in the same areas where digitsurface lumped semi-landmarks together" could be the reason and "non-decimated mesh with regularly spaced vertices to build the template helped correct this issue" (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/geomorph-r-package/digitsurface|sort:date/geomorph-r-package/_RqlvyC8LQ4/UvIbL7VZBQAJ). But I checked my mesh in MeshLab and did not seem to note lumped triangles.


2. Sherratt suggested that "specimen lack homologous points (fixed landmarks)" could be another reason (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/geomorph-r-package/digitsurface|sort:date/geomorph-r-package/yu4UyOhqZqc/X5kadFj3AAAJ). At first, I thought this could be an issue since I treated 20 curve semilandmarks as fixed landmarks. But the isssue did not resolve even I only used the 6 landmarks by specifying fixed = lmks_sample[1:6,,1] in the digitsurface function.


Original data with explanations of their contents are available via GitHub (https://github.com/Patricklv/digitsurface-function-question) so that with the code above, my errors could be replicated. I wish to know what should I do so that surface semilandmarks could be placed on my sample in roughly corresponding places as they are placed on my template.


Thanks.

1.

parts: I am not sure if the displacement of surface semilandmarks on the sample is due to the limited number of surface semilandmarks on the template. Any suggestions are welcome.

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] digitsuface function placing surface semilandmarks undesirably
parts:
Hi, 

I guess Geomorph may require some specific format of the ply files. I usually use the "Correspondent" function of the Landmark editor to put semilandmarks on my scans. Then I import the data into R and use Geomorph to pick up fixed and curvature semilandmarks and perform the Procrustes analysis and other statistical analyses. You can download the user manual of the Landmark editor online and check this function out.

Hope this helps!

Charles

parts:
Thank you very much for your suggestions of this alternative. I have also noted that such template registration work could be done using other software, Landmark Editor is surely one of them. I wish to do it in geomorph since I have a large dataset and wish to be more efficient.

Regarding the .ply files you mentioned, as far as I know, geomorph requires ascii ply format, which is the format I have. I am not sure if there is any other additional requirement regarding the ply file.

By the way, I tried to increase the number of surface semilandmarks (~3000) in my template, which unfortunately did not seem to have any effect of the location of surface semilandmarks placed on the sample (image shown below). Landmarks were displaced to the same place as they were when there were fewer surface semilandmarks on the template. I tried to dive into the source code for the digitsurface function but did not figure out where along the algorithm went wrong.

Thank you!
